newsitem.title: GERMANY: No question whether Waigel stays in office - Kohl.
newsitem.headline: No question whether Waigel stays in office - Kohl.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Wednesday there was no question whether Finance Minister Theo Waigel should stay in office, dismissing calls for his resignation over government plans to revalue Bundesbank assets.

"There is no need to question whether he will stay in office," Kohl told the Bundestag lower house of parliament, where opposition Social Democrats and Greens have proposed a motion calling for Waigel to step down.

Waigel reached a preliminary agreement with Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer on Tuesday in a retreat from an original plan to revalue central bank assets this year to help Germany qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
But in what the German media and opposition parties called an embarrassing climbdown, Waigel abandoned the plan aimed at plugging yawning gaps in the budget.

Addressing a parliament session due to vote on an opposition resolution to sack him, Waigel said he and Tietmeyer would do their best to have windfall revaluation profits transferred to Bonn's budget from 1998.
But Waigel did not make it clear whether gold or currency reserves or both were to be revalued. Tietmeyer has said the gold reserves were not under discussion during his talks with Waigel in Bonn.
